meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'чему').

examples.text: Шеф, а почему блюда такие маленькие?

And why is it so expensive?

examples.trans: I do not understand, why is the restaurant closed?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian conversational adverb meaning 'so', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Итак, в новом меню морские гребешки.
examples.trans: So, on the new menu are sea scallops.

examples.text: Шеф, а почему блюда такие маленькие?

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'рого'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: And why is it so expensive?
Hello, Vitya, are you going to feed me?

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'верное').

examples.trans: Probably, it is very rare.

examples.trans: I have very important news.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('rare').

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('normal').

examples.trans: Is there a normal restaurant nearby?
It's a decent job.
Normal jokes.

meanings.note: Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.text: Извините, но я решил остаться в ресторане.
examples.trans: Forgive me, but I decided to stay at the restaurant.
We are changing the restaurant's concept.

examples.trans: Is there a normal restaurant nearby?

examples.text: Костя сказал это совершенно поблизости и спокойно.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'there is'.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('new').

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian discourse particle adding conversational nuance meaning 'not', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'can, am able to', paired with 'смочь'.

meanings.en: to make up, to make peace
meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мириться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to make peace, reconcile', paired with 'мириться'.

examples.trans: I cannot make up with Katya.
I am agonizing and want to make up.

examples.text: Когда-нибудь ты захочешь помириться со своим папой.
examples.trans: Someday you will want to make up with your dad.

meanings.note: Formed with a diminutive/expressive Slavic suffix adding warmth or small scale. Common masculine noun meaning 'flowers' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: She throws away flowers and does not pick up the phone.
Very bad flowers.
He gave her beautiful flowers.

meanings.en: to throw out, to toss out
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'брасывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'throws away', paired with 'выбросить'.

examples.trans: She throws away flowers and does not pick up the phone.

examples.text: Иван Васильевич, выбрасывать человека в окно нормально?

meanings.en: to mock, to tease; colloquially 'are you kidding me?'
meanings.note: Prefix 'из-' ('out from within') marks extraction or exhaustion (stem 'деваться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'mock / kidding', paired with 'поиздеваться'.

examples.trans: Are you kidding me?
Stop messing with me!
Are you mocking me? — Well?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

meanings.en: to drink up, to have a drink
meanings.note: Prefix 'вы-' ('out of') marks outward movement or thorough completion (stem 'пить'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will drink', paired with 'выпивать'.

examples.text: Катя, я могу с тобой выпить?

examples.text: Тоже выпить со мной хочешь, да?
examples.trans: You want to have a drink with me too, right?

examples.text: Не знаю, например, выпить с ним чашечку кофе через час.
examples.trans: I do not know, for example, drink a cup of coffee with him in an hour.

meanings.note: Prefix 'рас-' ('apart, un-, thoroughly') indicates distribution or intensive action (stem 'слабиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'will relax', paired with 'расслабляться'.

examples.trans: Vanya, relax.

examples.text: Ваня, расслабься. В этот раз без обмана.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'оюзник'). Derived noun with agent/object suffix '-ник'/'-щик'/'-чик'. Common masculine noun meaning 'ally' in everyday Russian.
